Dead-stop high box step-up: Use a high box that creates roughly 90–110° knee flexion. Start completely still. Shift over the elevated foot and drive through that leg with minimal push from the floor foot. Stand fully, lower under control, reset before every rep.
Conventional deadlift: Bar over midfoot. Brace, set the lats, take slack out, then push the floor away. Keep the bar close. Use a normal controlled eccentric and strong concentric intent; reset on the floor.
Block deadlift: Deadlift from blocks/pins, usually below knee to mid-shin. Brace and set lats before each rep. Drive up with strong concentric intent; no deliberate slow eccentric or pause.
Front squat: Use a natural controlled descent and strong concentric intent. Keep the trunk stacked and elbows high.
Back squat: Use a natural controlled descent and strong concentric intent. Do not deliberately slow the eccentric.
Wide scapular isometric: Take a wider-than-normal pull-up grip with elbows straight. Depress/slightly retract the scapulae, creating a small body rise, and hold without hanging passively.
Offset pull-up lock-off: Use an uneven grip/assistance so one arm carries more load. Shift toward the primary arm, hold around 90° elbow flexion, then lower under control.
Dragon-flag negative: Anchor the upper body, maintain a rigid trunk and lower from the top position under control. Stop before lumbar position is lost.
Windmill: Hold the KB overhead, turn feet slightly away from the loaded arm, hinge/shift through the hip and reach the free hand down while keeping the loaded shoulder stacked.
Bear-plank DB drag: Hover knees just off the floor. Drag a DB under the torso with the opposite hand while resisting trunk/pelvic rotation.
FFE split squat: Elevate the front foot 2–4 inches. Descend down and forward through the front leg; allow useful knee travel while maintaining control.
Deficit reverse lunge: Stand on a small platform and step the working-side partner leg backward off it to create extra front-leg ROM.
Heavy suitcase march: Carry a heavy DB/KB on one side and march slowly, resisting side bend and rotation.
Pullover-to-press: Perform a DB pullover, return over the chest, then perform a chest press; that sequence is one rep.
Assisted wide lock-off eccentric: Use a pull-up bar with a box, band, or light help from the opposite arm. Start near the top with the working hand wider than shoulder width. Shift most of your weight to that arm, hold the bent-arm position for 1–2 seconds, then slowly straighten that arm over about 3–5 seconds. Keep the shoulder pulled down and active rather than shrugging toward the ear.
Ab-wheel rollout: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders. Tuck the pelvis slightly and brace your abs as if preparing for a punch. Roll forward by letting the shoulders travel ahead while the hips follow, keeping ribs down and avoiding a low-back arch. Go only as far as you can keep that trunk position, then use the abs and lats to pull back.
Banded backward hamstring raise: Anchor a band in front of you and loop it around one ankle. Face the anchor and, with the knee mostly straight, drive that leg backward from the hip against the band. Keep the pelvis square and trunk still; do not create the motion by arching your low back. Return slowly until the leg is under you.
Chest-supported DB row: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Start with arms hanging. Pull the elbows back toward the hips/ribs while keeping your chest on the pad and shoulders away from your ears. Pause briefly when the upper arms reach the torso, then lower until the arms are straight.
Very high box step-up: Use a box high enough that the working hip and knee are deeply flexed. Place the whole working foot on the box, lean the torso slightly over that leg, and shift your weight onto it before pushing. Stand by driving through the elevated leg with as little help as possible from the floor leg. Lower under control.
DB bench press: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Set the shoulder blades gently back/down, feet planted. Lower the dumbbells toward the sides of the chest with forearms roughly vertical, then press them up and slightly inward without letting the shoulders roll forward.
Weighted pull-up: Attach weight with a belt or hold it securely. Start from an active hang with shoulders engaged. Pull by driving the elbows down until the chin clears the bar or the chest approaches it, without kicking or swinging. Lower to straight arms under control while keeping the shoulders active.
Weighted dead bug: Lie on your back with hips and knees at 90 degrees and hold a light weight above the chest. Flatten the low back gently into the floor by bringing ribs toward pelvis. Slowly extend one leg while keeping the trunk completely still, return, and alternate. Stop the leg before the low back lifts.
Hanging pelvic-tilt knee raise: Hang from a bar with shoulders active. Before lifting the knees, curl the pelvis upward by shortening the distance between the ribs and pelvis. Continue bringing the knees toward the chest without swinging. Lower under control and return to a stable hang before the next rep.
Side plank + top-leg raise: Set a side plank on the forearm with body in a straight line. Lift the hips and keep ribs and pelvis stacked. Without rolling backward, raise the top leg from the hip, pause, lower it, and maintain the plank throughout.
Romanian deadlift (RDL): Hold the bar at the thighs with knees slightly bent. Push the hips backward while keeping the bar close to the legs and spine neutral. Lower until you reach your available hamstring range without rounding, then drive the hips forward to stand. The knees stay relatively fixed rather than turning it into a squat.
1-arm DB row: Support yourself with the opposite hand on a bench or rack. Let the dumbbell hang, brace the trunk, then pull the elbow toward the hip while keeping the shoulder away from the ear. Avoid twisting the torso to finish the rep. Lower to a long arm under control.
1-arm DB floor press: Lie on your back with one dumbbell. Bend the knees and brace so the torso does not rotate. Lower the upper arm until the triceps lightly contacts the floor, then press the dumbbell upward while keeping ribs down and shoulder controlled.
Wide lateral lunge: Take a wide stance or step laterally. Sit the hips back and bend one knee while the opposite leg stays long. Keep the working foot planted and knee tracking over the foot. Push through the bent leg to return to center.
Front-rack contralateral carry: Hold one kettlebell or dumbbell in a front-rack position at one shoulder. Walk slowly while keeping ribs stacked over pelvis. Resist leaning or rotating toward or away from the weight. Switch sides after the prescribed time.
Long-lever body saw: Start in a forearm plank with elbows slightly farther in front of the shoulders than usual. Brace glutes and abs so the body stays rigid. Shift the whole body backward and then forward without changing spinal position. The farther the elbows are from the shoulders, the harder the abdominal demand.
Bottoms-up KB carry: Hold a light kettlebell upside down so the bell is above the handle. Keep wrist vertical and elbow near 90 degrees or slightly higher. Walk slowly while keeping the bell balanced and shoulder stable. Use a lighter load than a normal carry.
Weighted pike lift: Sit with legs straight in front of you and torso tall. Place hands beside or slightly ahead of the thighs. Compress the thighs toward the torso and lift one or both heels off the floor without leaning far backward. Add ankle weights or lift over a small object when bodyweight is easy.
1-arm supported row: Brace one hand on a bench/rack and hold a dumbbell in the other. Keep hips and shoulders square. Pull the dumbbell toward the lower ribs/hip, pause without rotating, then lower until the arm is long.
Archer/offset pull-up: Take a wider grip than a normal pull-up. Pull your body toward one hand while that elbow bends strongly and the opposite arm stays straighter, as if performing an assisted one-arm pull-up. Return to center under control and repeat to the other side or complete all reps on one side.
Wide pull-up isometric + eccentric: Take a wide pull-up grip and use a box or assistance to reach a bent-arm position. Hold with shoulders active for the prescribed time. Then perform the prescribed slow lowerings, taking about 3–5 seconds to reach straight arms without dropping into a passive shoulder hang.
Cossack squat: Take a very wide stance. Shift your hips toward one leg and bend that knee deeply while the other leg stays long; the straight-leg toes may turn upward if needed. Keep the working foot planted and chest controlled. Drive through the bent leg to return to center.
Weighted chin-up: Use an underhand shoulder-width grip and attach weight securely. Start from an active hang. Pull the elbows down/back until the chin clears the bar, keeping the trunk controlled. Lower to full elbow extension without swinging.
Half-kneeling 1-arm DB press: Kneel on one knee with the opposite foot forward. Hold a dumbbell at the shoulder on either side as prescribed, squeeze the glute of the down-knee side, and keep ribs stacked. Press overhead without leaning sideways or arching the low back, then lower to the shoulder.
Archer DB row: Set up in a supported or hinged row position with one dumbbell. As you row, let the elbow travel outward more than in a standard row, aiming toward the upper ribs. Keep the torso controlled and shoulder away from the ear; lower to full reach.
Heavy farmer carry: Hold a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand. Stand tall with ribs stacked, shoulders active, and hands beside the thighs. Walk with controlled steps without shrugging, swaying, or letting the weights pull the shoulders forward.
Neutral-grip scapular pull: Hang from parallel/neutral handles with elbows straight. Without bending the arms, pull the shoulder blades down so the body rises slightly. Pause, then return toward the hang under control. The movement is small and comes from the shoulder blades.
Hanging straight-leg raise: Hang from a bar with shoulders active and legs straight. Brace the trunk and lift the legs in front of you without swinging, aiming toward hip height or higher while curling the pelvis slightly at the top. Lower slowly.
Single-leg hip thrust: Place the upper back on a bench and one foot on the floor. Lift the other foot. Drive through the planted foot to raise the hips until the torso and thigh form a straight line. Keep ribs down and finish with the glute rather than arching the low back.
Bear-plank shoulder tap: Start on hands and knees, then hover the knees 1–2 inches above the floor. Brace hard and lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder. Keep hips and shoulders as still as possible. Alternate sides.
Heel-elevated front squat: Place heels on small plates or a wedge and hold the bar in front-rack position. Squat down between the legs, allowing the knees to travel forward while keeping the whole foot supported and elbows high. Drive up through the feet without letting the torso collapse.
Incline chest-supported DB row: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging. Pull the elbows back toward the ribs while keeping the chest against the pad. Avoid shrugging. Lower until the arms are straight and shoulder blades can move naturally.
Bulgarian split squat: Place the rear foot on a bench and the front foot far enough forward to stay balanced. Lower mostly straight down through the front leg until comfortable depth, keeping the front foot planted. Drive through the front leg to stand; use the rear leg mainly for balance.
Incline DB press: Lie on an incline bench with dumbbells at the upper chest. Set the shoulders, lower the weights with forearms roughly vertical, then press up and slightly inward. Keep ribs controlled rather than over-arching to finish.
Neutral-grip pull-up: Use parallel handles with palms facing each other. Begin in an active hang, pull the elbows toward the ribs until the chin reaches hand height, then lower under control to straight arms without swinging.
Hollow pullover hold: Lie on your back holding a dumbbell with both hands above the chest. Bring ribs toward pelvis and lightly lift or position the legs so the low back stays controlled. Lower the weight behind the head until just before the ribs flare or back arches, then hold for the prescribed time.
Loaded Cossack squat: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest. Take a wide stance and sink toward one leg while the other stays straight. Keep the working foot planted and use the load as counterbalance. Drive back to center and repeat on the other side.
Cross-body dead-bug press: Lie on your back with hips/knees at 90 degrees and a dumbbell in one hand above the chest. Brace the trunk, then extend the leg opposite the loaded arm while maintaining the press and keeping the low back from arching. Return and repeat before switching sides.
Straight-arm DB pullover: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell with both hands over the chest. Keep a small fixed elbow bend. Lower the weight in an arc behind the head while keeping ribs down, then use the lats/chest to bring it back over the chest without changing elbow angle much.
Side-plank DB row: Set a side plank facing an anchored dumbbell setup or perform from a supported side-plank position where the free arm can row. Maintain a straight body and stable pelvis while pulling the weight toward the ribs. Do not rotate the torso to create the row.
B-stance RDL: Stand with most weight on the front leg and place the other foot slightly behind as a kickstand. Hinge the hips backward over the working leg with a soft knee, keeping the weight close. Feel the working hamstring load, then drive that hip forward to stand; the rear foot provides balance, not equal force.
Seal/incline row: Lie chest-down on a flat elevated bench for a seal row, or on an incline bench if that setup is easier. Let the weights hang, then row toward the ribs without lifting the chest or using hip momentum. Lower to straight arms.
Barbell hip thrust: Sit with upper back against a bench and bar padded across the hips. Plant feet about hip-width. Drive through the feet to lift the hips until torso and thighs are roughly level, keeping ribs down and chin tucked. Squeeze glutes at the top without hyperextending the low back.
Weighted ring push-up: Set rings low and add load with a vest/plate or other secure method. Keep the body rigid. Lower the chest between the rings while allowing the hands to rotate naturally, then press back up while keeping the rings controlled close to the body.
Lateral step-up: Stand beside a box with the working foot on top. Shift the hips over that foot and push through the elevated leg to stand on the box, minimizing push from the floor leg. Lower laterally under control.
Offset front-rack march: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell in the front-rack position on one side only. Stand tall and alternate lifting the knees as in a slow march. Keep pelvis level and resist rotation or side bending toward the load.
Towel/neutral-grip lock-off: Hang from a towel or neutral-grip handles. Pull into a bent-arm position, usually around 90 degrees, and hold while keeping the shoulder down and active. Use assistance if needed to maintain the position without twisting or losing shoulder control.
Heavy overhead suitcase hold: Press one dumbbell or kettlebell overhead and hold it there while standing tall. Keep the elbow locked or nearly locked, shoulder actively upward/stable, ribs down, and pelvis level. Resist leaning away from the weight.
Weighted reverse crunch: Lie on your back and secure a light load between the feet/knees or use ankle weights. Start with hips/knees bent. Curl the pelvis off the floor toward the ribs rather than simply swinging the knees toward the chest. Lower the pelvis slowly.
Copenhagen plank: Lie on your side with the top leg supported on a bench at the knee or ankle. Prop on the lower forearm and lift the hips so the body forms a straight line. Bring the lower leg up toward the bench or let it hover. Hold without rotating.
Zercher squat: Cradle the bar in the crooks of the elbows with hands together or forearms up. Brace and squat between the legs while keeping the bar close to the torso. Drive through the feet to stand; keep the upper back from rounding excessively.
Weighted ring row: Set rings around waist-to-chest height and place the body underneath them. Add a vest/plate or elevate the feet. Keep the body rigid, pull the chest toward the rings with elbows driving back, then lower to straight arms without sagging at the hips.
High step-up from dead stop: Place one foot on a high box and begin completely still with the other foot on the floor. Shift your center of mass over the elevated foot before pushing. Stand using the box leg with minimal assistance from the trailing foot, then lower and fully reset.
Weighted push-up: Add load with a vest, plate secured on the upper back, or bands. Keep a straight line from shoulders through hips. Lower the chest between the hands with elbows at a comfortable angle, then press the floor away without letting the hips sag or ribs flare.
Towel pull-up: Drape one or two sturdy towels over a pull-up bar and grip the ends. Start from an active hang, squeeze the towels firmly, and pull until the hands/chin reach the top position. Lower under control. Use assistance if grip fails before the intended pulling stimulus.
Offset front-rack hold: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell in front-rack position on one side only. Stand still with ribs over pelvis and both feet evenly loaded. Resist rotation and side bending for the prescribed time, then switch sides.
Loaded side-plank row: Hold a side plank while rowing a dumbbell or band with the top arm. Pull toward the ribs without allowing the pelvis or shoulders to rotate. Maintain the plank from feet/knees through the head throughout each rep.
Weighted dead-bug pullover: Lie on your back with hips/knees at 90 degrees and hold a dumbbell over the chest with both hands. Brace so the low back stays controlled. Lower the dumbbell behind the head while simultaneously maintaining the dead-bug position; stop before ribs flare, then pull the weight back over the chest.
L-sit tuck hold/lift: Support yourself on parallettes, rings, or sturdy handles with arms straight. Push the shoulders down, tuck the knees toward the chest, and lift the feet off the floor. Either hold that position or repeatedly lift/lower the tucked legs without collapsing through the shoulders.
1-arm incline DB press: Lie on an incline bench with one dumbbell at the upper chest. Brace the trunk so the torso does not rotate toward the weight. Press overhead/forward along the bench angle, then lower under control while keeping the shoulder centered.
FFE reverse lunge: Stand with the front foot elevated 2–4 inches. Step the other leg backward into a lunge, allowing extra depth through the front hip and knee. Keep the front foot planted and drive through that leg to return to standing.
1-arm high row: Support the torso as needed and hold one dumbbell. Row with the elbow traveling outward and upward toward the upper ribs rather than tight to the hip. Keep the shoulder away from the ear and avoid rotating the trunk.
Wide-grip pull-up: Grip the bar wider than shoulder width but within a pain-free range. Start from an active hang and pull the chest upward by driving the elbows down. Do not force an excessively wide position or shrug at the bottom. Lower under control.
Heavy suitcase deadlift: Place a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell beside one foot. Hinge and bend the knees enough to grasp it while keeping shoulders and hips square. Brace against the uneven load, stand by driving through both feet, then lower it beside the foot without leaning toward the weight.
Incline rear-delt row: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with light-to-moderate dumbbells. Row with elbows flared roughly 60–90 degrees from the torso, aiming the weights toward the upper ribs. Squeeze the rear shoulders/upper back without shrugging, then lower.
Weighted decline sit-up: Secure the feet on a decline bench and hold a weight at the chest. Start reclined with the trunk controlled, then curl/sit up using the abdominals without yanking through the neck. Lower under control to the starting angle.
Cross-body suitcase carry: Hold one heavy dumbbell or kettlebell at your side. Walk while actively resisting the load's attempt to bend you sideways; think of the opposite-side trunk staying engaged across the body. Keep shoulders and pelvis level, then switch hands.
Heel-elevated goblet squat: Elevate the heels on plates or a wedge and hold a dumbbell/kettlebell at the chest. Squat down between the legs, allowing knees to travel forward while keeping the feet supported. Stay tall through the torso and drive through the feet to stand.
Ring archer row: Set up for a ring row. As you pull, bend one arm strongly while the other arm opens straighter to the side, shifting the chest toward the working hand. Keep the body rigid. Return to center and alternate or finish one side before switching.
Walking lunge: Step forward into a lunge and lower until both legs are comfortably bent. Push through the front foot and bring the rear leg forward directly into the next step. Keep the pelvis controlled and front knee tracking with the foot.
Chaos push-up/press: For a chaos push-up, loop a strong resistance band horizontally across a rack and place the hands on the suspended band. Perform push-ups while controlling the band's instability. Keep the body rigid and use a setup that cannot slip; reduce instability if shoulder position becomes uncontrolled.
Mixed-grip pull-up: Use two different hand orientations or implements, such as one overhand and one neutral/towel grip. Pull with the torso square and avoid rotating toward the stronger grip. Complete the prescribed reps, then reverse the grips so each side gets both positions.
Weighted pike compression: Sit with straight legs and a weight/ankle weights as appropriate. Place hands beside the thighs, keep the knees straight, and actively pull the thighs toward the torso while lifting the heels from the floor. Lower with control without leaning far backward.
KB press in wide side lunge: Take a wide stance and sink into a lateral lunge on one side. Hold a kettlebell at the shoulder, stabilize the lunge, then press it overhead while keeping ribs stacked and the loaded shoulder controlled. Lower the bell before coming out of the lunge.
Hanging diagonal knee raise: Hang with shoulders active. Curl the pelvis and bring both knees upward toward one side of the torso rather than straight to the chest. Lower without swinging, then alternate sides or complete the prescribed reps on one side.
Long-lever glute bridge: Lie on your back with heels farther from the hips than in a normal bridge. Brace the trunk and drive through the heels to lift the hips. Keep ribs down and feel the hamstrings/glutes; do not finish by arching the low back.
Ab-wheel extended start: Begin the ab-wheel rollout with the wheel positioned slightly farther in front of the shoulders than in a standard start. Brace hard, roll farther forward only while ribs and pelvis remain controlled, then pull back using the abs/lats. Use a shorter range if the low back arches.
Barbell hinge from blocks: Set the bar on blocks or pins around mid-shin to just below knee height. With feet under the hips, hinge back to the bar, brace and set the lats, then stand by extending the hips. Lower by pushing the hips back until the bar returns to the blocks. Treat it as a shortened-range deadlift/hinge, not a squat.
Prone incline Y-row: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with light dumbbells. Raise the arms in a Y-shaped path, thumbs generally upward, pulling the shoulder blades upward/back without shrugging aggressively. Use light loads and keep the movement controlled.
Elevated reverse lunge: Stand on a small platform. Step one leg backward off the platform and descend into a reverse lunge, using the elevation to gain additional range. Keep the front foot planted and push through the front leg to return to the platform.
Standing 1-arm DB press: Stand with one dumbbell at shoulder height. Brace glutes and abs, keep ribs over pelvis, and press the dumbbell overhead without leaning sideways or arching. Finish with the arm overhead and shoulder stable, then lower to the shoulder.
Loaded frog bridge: Lie on your back, place the soles of the feet together and let the knees fall outward. Place a dumbbell/plate across the hips. Brace the trunk and squeeze the glutes to lift the hips, pause at the top without arching the back, then lower.
Chest-supported high row: Lie chest-down on an incline bench. Row dumbbells toward the upper ribs/chest with elbows angled outward rather than tucked. Keep the chest on the pad and shoulders away from the ears. Lower to full reach.
Mixed/offset grip lock-off: Use unequal grips—such as one normal bar grip and one towel/offset grip—so the arms have different demands. Pull into a controlled bent-arm lock-off and hold without rotating the torso. Reverse the grip arrangement so both sides train each role.
Cross-body overhead carry: Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell overhead. Walk slowly while keeping the loaded arm stacked over the shoulder and ribs over pelvis. Resist rotation and side bending through the opposite side of the trunk. Switch arms after the prescribed distance/time.
Straight-leg hanging raise: Hang from a bar with shoulders active. Keep knees straight and raise the legs forward by flexing at the hips and curling the pelvis, without swinging. Lift as high as you can maintain control, then lower slowly.
Front-rack step-up: Hold one or two weights in front-rack position and place one foot fully on a box. Shift your weight over the elevated foot, drive through that leg to stand on the box, and minimize push from the trailing foot. Lower under control.
1-arm chest-supported row: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and row one dumbbell at a time. Keep the chest and pelvis on the bench so you cannot rotate. Pull the elbow toward the ribs/hip, then lower until the arm is long.
Wide eccentric pull-up: Take a wide but pain-free grip. Use a box or assistance to start at the top of a pull-up, then lower yourself slowly over about 3–5 seconds while keeping shoulders active. Step back up for the next rep rather than pulling up if the exercise is prescribed as eccentric-only.
Turkish sit-up: Lie on your back with a kettlebell or dumbbell pressed vertically in one hand, same-side knee bent and opposite leg straight. Keep eyes on the weight. Roll onto the opposite forearm, then press up onto that hand while keeping the loaded arm vertical. Reverse the steps back to the floor; this is the first portion of a Turkish get-up.
Weighted side-plank hip lift: Set a side plank with a weight resting securely on the top hip. Lower the hips a controlled distance toward the floor, then drive them back up until the body forms a straight line. Keep the torso from rotating.
Weighted ring dip / pain-free dip: Support yourself above parallel rings or dip bars with shoulders active. Add weight only if bodyweight is comfortable. Lower by bending the elbows until the shoulder reaches a pain-free depth, then press back to straight arms. On rings, keep them close and controlled; do not force deep shoulder extension.
Loaded lateral lunge: Hold a dumbbell, kettlebell, or barbell securely. Step or shift laterally, sit the hips back over the working leg, and keep the opposite leg long. Drive through the working foot to return to center without the knee collapsing inward.
Offset/archer row: Use rings, a cable/band substitute, or dumbbell setup that lets one arm do more of the pulling. Shift toward the working arm as it bends while the other arm stays straighter. Keep the trunk controlled and reverse sides so each arm takes the primary role.
Neutral-grip weighted pull-up: Attach weight securely and use parallel handles with palms facing each other. Start in an active hang, pull the elbows down until the chin clears hand height, then lower under control to straight arms without swinging.
Heavy front-rack march: Hold heavy kettlebells/dumbbells in front-rack position, or use the prescribed single-sided rack. Stand tall and slowly alternate lifting each knee. Keep ribs stacked, pelvis level, and avoid leaning or rotating as the foot leaves the floor.
